title: Local models and constructible sheaves
statement:
The definition of a constructible sheaf makes sense for any condensed ring. Recall that for
$g\colon Z\to X$ the restriction $M|_Z=g^*M$ of a $\Lambda_X$-module is a
$\Lambda_Z$-module, since $g^{-1}\Lambda_X\simeq\Lambda_Z$
([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], [sk-def-sfb-transport]); thus
$g^*\colon\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring.

1. A $\Lambda_X$-module $M$ has a *finite constant local model* if there is a pro-étale
   cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]) and finitely presented modules $P_i$
   over the scalar ring $\Lambda(*)$ such that
   $$
   M|_{U_i}\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i .
   $$
   Here $\Lambda(*)$ and $P_i$ are constant sheaves on $U_i$, acting through
   $\Lambda(*)\to\Lambda_{U_i}$. Equivalently, on each $U_i$ the module $M$ has a
   presentation by a finite matrix with entries in the scalar ring $\Lambda(*)$.
2. For qcqs $X$, a $\Lambda_X$-module $M$ is *constructible* if there is a finite
   stratification $X=\coprod_aX_a$ by constructible locally closed subschemes
   ([def-constructible-stratification]) such that each $M|_{X_a}$ has a finite constant
   local model. On an arbitrary scheme this condition is imposed locally on affine opens.
   The word constructible requires each stratum to be a constructible subset; for
   Noetherian schemes this is automatic for locally closed strata.

We write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)\subset\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory
of constructible sheaves, and $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)\subset D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ for the
full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves (compare
[sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]). A complex $K$ has *Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$* if
$K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}N$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ for every sheaf $N$ of
$\Lambda_X$-modules. We write $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of
$\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ of complexes of finite Tor amplitude (compare [sk-def-sf-categories]).

proof.text: For a morphism $g\colon Z\to X$, the coefficient rings are $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and $\Lambda_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The map $\alpha_g\colon g^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_Z$ is an isomorphism for every condensed ring [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. The module pullback of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] is $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_g}\operatorname{mapMod}(g^{-1})$. The transport functor in [sk-def-sfb-transport] gives a module over $g^{-1}\Lambda_X$, and the module-pullback statement gives the extension of scalars its codomain $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Z}$. Together with the coefficient isomorphism this justifies the restriction notation in the definition for arbitrary $\Lambda$.

source.place: Introductory paragraph; proof paragraph 1, restriction and module transport

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] in $\mathcal C=\Ab$ with $R=\Lambda(*)$: the scalar module $P_i$ has a finite presentation $R^{m_i}\to R^{n_i}\to P_i\to0$. The scalar-to-coefficient map and the meaning $\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i=\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)_{U_i}}(P_i)_{U_i}$ are given in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. That node's equivalence (1)–(2) gives precisely the matrix description in part (1), with entries in the scalar ring. This uses the finite constant local model predicate, rather than identifying it with arbitrary local finite presentation.

source.place: Part (1); proof paragraph 2, finite constant local models and matrices

proof.text: Take a finite stratification in the sense of [def-constructible-stratification] and require, in addition, that every stratum image is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. On a qcqs scheme impose the finite constant local model predicate of part (1) on each restriction to a stratum; on a general scheme impose the stated condition on affine opens. This is the definition in part (2). The Noetherian remark follows from the cited constructible-subset statement: in a Noetherian space every finite union of locally closed subsets is constructible, so each single locally closed stratum is constructible.

Use the ambient module category and its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and its relative derived tensor product $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Form the full subcategory $\operatorname{Cons}$ on the modules satisfying part (2). Form $\Dbc$ on the complexes for which $H^q=0$ outside a finite interval and every $H^q$ belongs to $\operatorname{Cons}$. For $a\leq b$, impose $H^q(K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ and every module sheaf $N$ placed in degree zero. Existentially quantifying $a,b$ defines finite Tor amplitude, and imposing it on the objects of $\Dbc$ defines $\Dctf$. Each full subcategory keeps exactly the ambient morphisms; these are direct definitions and require no stability or triangulatedness assertion.

source.place: Final paragraph, definitions of Cons, Dbc, Tor amplitude and Dctf; proof paragraph 2

proof_origin.place: Statement parts (1), (2), final paragraph; sk-def-sfb-constructible.proof.md, both paragraphs, with the local-finite-presentation mismatch and forward-reference cycles repaired

lean.note: Missing dependency supplied in this delivery. The node has no recorded declaration or Mathlib match. Upstream IsConstructibleModuleObject uses arbitrary local finite-presentation matrices, whereas this node requires finite constant scalar models and the affine-local convention on general schemes. The module states exactly that notion: finite presentations are chosen over the condensed coefficient ring on the point, before pullback to each member of the cover, so their matrices have entries in Λ(*); it also defines Cons, Dbc and Dctf using the existing ordinary derived category and generic Tor-amplitude predicates.
